place.source_title: St. Gabriel's Church (Roman Catholic), 4522 South Wallace Street

brief: Big Romanesque Revival brick church of 1887 for the Polish parish near the rail yards: a broad gabled front with a large rose window over three arched doors, a massive square corner tower with a pyramidal cap, round-arched side windows, and an ornate carved altar inside; the parish school stands alongside.

facade.notes: St. Gabriel's (Chicago, Canaryville, 1887; Burnham and Root), HABS: a brown-brick Romanesque church -- a big gable with a rose window over three arched portals on a broad flight of steps, a tall square tower with round corner turrets and conical caps at one side; iron fence along the sidewalk

why.note: a church is a long nave pointed at the street with a tower marking the entrance
the parish church of a Chicago stockyard neighbourhood: the biggest building for blocks around
